title: Listening at natural speed
description: Friends, family, neighbours, doctors and staff at natural speed, with the casual speech you'll really hear: nggak, udah, aja, kok, sih. Hear a line, pick what it means, and learn a reply.

items.speaker: friend
items.indonesian: Udah makan belum?
items.english: Have you eaten yet?

reply.english: Yes, earlier. You?

items.note: Belum at the end makes it 'yet or not?'. Answer udah or belum, not ya or nggak.

items.speaker: friend
items.indonesian: Kok nggak bilang-bilang mau ke Bali?
items.english: How come you didn't tell me you were going to Bali?

reply.english: Sorry, it was all a bit last-minute.

items.note: Bilang is the spoken 'say'; said twice, it's 'say a word about it', with a hint of hurt feelings.

items.speaker: friend
items.indonesian: Nanti malam jadi nonton, nggak?
items.english: Are we still going to the film tonight?

reply.english: Of course! Seven, right?

items.note: Jadi here means 'going ahead as planned', and nggak at the end makes it a yes-or-no question.

items.speaker: friend
items.indonesian: Aku telat dikit, ya. Masih di jalan.
items.english: I'll be a bit late. I'm still on the way.

reply.indonesian: Oke, santai aja. Aku tunggu di dalam.
reply.english: OK, no rush. I'll wait inside.

items.note: Telat is the spoken terlambat, and dikit is sedikit with the se- dropped.

items.speaker: friend
items.indonesian: Aduh, maaf banget, aku nggak jadi ikut. Ada urusan mendadak.
items.english: Oh, I'm really sorry, I can't come after all. Something's come up.

reply.indonesian: Yah, sayang banget. Ya udah, lain kali, ya.
reply.english: Oh, what a shame. Never mind, next time.

items.note: Nggak jadi means a plan is off. Urusan, 'business', is a reason nobody questions.

items.speaker: friend
items.indonesian: Gimana, enak nggak?
items.english: So? Is it good?

reply.english: It's so good! You've got to try it.

items.note: Gimana on its own asks for your verdict: 'Well? How is it?'.

items.speaker: friend
items.indonesian: Kamu kok kelihatan capek banget, sih?
items.english: How come you look so tired?

reply.english: Yeah, I couldn't sleep last night.

items.note: Kok asks with surprise and sih softens it: concern, not criticism.

items.speaker: friend
items.indonesian: Mau aku jemput, nggak?
items.english: Do you want me to pick you up?

reply.indonesian: Nggak usah, aku naik ojek aja.
reply.english: No need, I'll just get an ojek.

items.speaker: friend
items.indonesian: Bagus, kok. Cocok sama kamu.
items.english: It looks good, honestly. It suits you.

reply.english: Really? Thanks.

items.note: Kok at the end reassures: 'it really does'. Sama is the spoken dengan (with).

items.speaker: friend
items.indonesian: Kamu udah pernah ke Lombok, belum?
items.english: Have you ever been to Lombok?

reply.english: No, never. Is it nice?

items.note: The no to udah pernah …? is belum pernah, 'not yet', which leaves the door open.

items.speaker: friend
items.indonesian: Ini HP kamu, bukan? Ketinggalan di meja.
items.english: Isn't this your phone? You left it on the table.

reply.english: Oh no, it is! Thanks so much.

items.note: HP (ha-pe) is the everyday word for a mobile phone. Ketinggalan is left behind by accident.
items.audioHint: Ini ha pe kamu, bukan? Ketinggalan di meja.

items.speaker: friend
items.indonesian: Hari ini aku yang traktir, ya.
items.english: Today's on me.

reply.indonesian: Wah, makasih! Lain kali gantian, ya.
reply.english: Oh, thanks! Next time it's my turn.

items.note: Traktir is treating someone to food or drinks. Friends take turns, or split the bill: patungan.

items.speaker: mother
items.indonesian: Udah, nggak usah dicuci. Taruh aja di situ.
items.english: Oh, don't bother washing up. Just leave it there.

reply.indonesian: Tidak apa-apa, Tante. Biar saya bantu.
reply.english: It's no trouble. Let me help.

items.note: Hosts always wave the offer away, and offering is what counts. She can talk casually to you; you still answer politely.

items.speaker: mother
items.indonesian: Kok makannya sedikit? Nggak suka, ya?
items.english: Why are you eating so little? Don't you like it?

reply.indonesian: Suka sekali, Tante. Tadi siang saya makan banyak.
reply.english: I love it. I just had a big lunch.

items.note: A light eater worries a host. Praise the food and give a reason.

items.speaker: mother
items.indonesian: Hati-hati di jalan, ya. Kalau udah sampai, kabarin.
items.english: Take care on the way. Let us know when you get home.

reply.english: I will. I'll message when I'm there.

items.note: Kabarin is the casual kabari, 'send word'. Families do wait for that message.

items.speaker: father
items.indonesian: Udah lama di Indonesia? Kok bahasanya lancar.
items.english: Have you been in Indonesia long? Your Indonesian's so fluent.

reply.indonesian: Baru dua tahun, Om. Masih belajar.
reply.english: Only two years. I'm still learning.

items.note: Playing it down with masih belajar is the gracious way to take a compliment.

items.speaker: mother
items.indonesian: Nginep sini aja, udah malam.
items.english: Why don't you stay the night? It's late.

reply.indonesian: Terima kasih, Tante, tapi besok saya kerja pagi.
reply.english: Thank you, but I'm working early tomorrow.

items.note: Nginep is the spoken menginap, to stay the night. Thanks and a reason make a kind no.

items.speaker: neighbour
items.indonesian: Mau ke mana, Sam? Kok rapi banget.
items.english: Where are you off to, Sam? You're all dressed up.

reply.english: To a friend's wedding.

items.note: Rapi, neat and tidy, is how you look when you're dressed up. Neighbours notice, and say so.

items.speaker: neighbour
items.indonesian: Katanya nanti malam mati lampu, lho.
items.english: Apparently there's going to be a power cut tonight.

reply.indonesian: Oh, ya? Dari jam berapa, Bu?
reply.english: Oh, really? From what time?

items.note: Katanya is 'apparently, I heard'. Mati lampu, 'the lights die', is a power cut.

items.speaker: neighbour
items.indonesian: Ini ada kue sedikit, buat icip-icip.
items.english: Here are a few cakes, just for you to try.

reply.indonesian: Wah, kok repot-repot, Bu? Terima kasih banyak.
reply.english: Oh, you shouldn't have! Thank you so much.

items.note: Kok repot-repot? (why go to the trouble?) is how you accept graciously. Return the plate later with something on it, not empty.

items.speaker: neighbour
items.indonesian: Airnya mati dari pagi. Di rumahmu juga?
items.english: The water's been off since this morning. At your place too?

reply.english: Yes, same here. I wonder why.

items.note: -mu is the short, casual 'your': rumahmu, your house. An older neighbour may use it with you; answer with Bu or Pak.

items.speaker: doctor
items.indonesian: Ada riwayat penyakit? Darah tinggi, asma?
items.english: Any medical history? High blood pressure, asthma?

reply.english: No, nothing.

items.note: Riwayat penyakit is your medical history; the doctor lists a few common ones to prompt you.

items.speaker: doctor
items.indonesian: Tensinya agak tinggi, ya. Kurangi garam.
items.english: Your blood pressure's a bit high. Cut down on salt.

reply.english: All right. Do I need medicine?

items.note: Tensi, blood pressure, is taken at almost every clinic visit.

items.speaker: doctor
items.indonesian: Antibiotiknya dihabiskan, ya, walaupun udah enakan.
items.english: Finish the antibiotics, even once you feel better.

reply.english: All right. Every last one.

items.note: Enakan is casual for 'feeling better', and doctors use it too. Dihabiskan is 'finished off', used up.

items.speaker: pharmacist
items.indonesian: Obat ini bikin ngantuk, jadi jangan nyetir, ya.
items.english: This medicine makes you drowsy, so don't drive.

reply.indonesian: Oh, oke. Diminum malam aja, ya?
reply.english: Oh, OK. Should I take it at night, then?

items.note: Bikin is the spoken membuat (to make), and nyetir is menyetir, to drive.

items.speaker: doctor
items.indonesian: Sakitnya di sebelah mana?
items.english: Where exactly does it hurt?

reply.indonesian: Di sini, Dok. Kalau ditekan, sakit.
reply.english: Here. It hurts when you press it.

items.note: Sebelah mana, 'which side', asks for the exact spot.

items.speaker: clerk
items.indonesian: Yang ini lagi diskon, Kak. Beli dua gratis satu.
items.english: This one's on offer. Buy two, get one free.

reply.indonesian: Oh, ya? Oke, saya ambil dua.
reply.english: Oh, really? OK, I'll take two.

items.note: Lagi here is 'at the moment': lagi diskon, lagi promo.

items.speaker: server
items.indonesian: Gulanya normal atau dikurangi, Kak?
items.english: Normal sugar, or less?

reply.english: Less, please.

items.note: Drinks come very sweet unless you ask. Cafés often say it in English: less sugar, less ice.

items.speaker: driver
items.indonesian: Udah sesuai titik, ya, Kak. Bintang limanya jangan lupa.
items.english: Here we are, right at the pin. Don't forget the five stars.

reply.english: Will do. Thanks.

items.note: Titik is the pin on the map. Drivers depend on their ratings, so many ask for five stars.

items.speaker: clerk
items.indonesian: Mohon maaf, sistemnya lagi error. Bisa ditunggu sebentar?
items.english: Sorry, the system's down at the moment. Could you wait a moment?

reply.english: Oh, that's fine. I'll wait.

items.note: Error is said as in English. Lagi (right now) turns up in polite staff talk too.
